Charging and discharging an RC circuit

Animation of an RC circuit. Circuit diagram: a battery (EMF) on the left, a two-way switch S at the top left that can touch contact a on the top wire or contact b on a wire to the bottom rail, a resistor R on the top wire and a capacitor C on the right. Current is drawn as a thick coloured line along the wires with arrowheads showing its direction; the line gets thinner as the current decays in steps of tau = RC. Plus signs above the top capacitor plate and minus signs below the bottom plate show the stored charge. First the switch swings to contact a: a clockwise current from the battery charges the capacitor over ten steps from t = 0 to 9 tau; the current line thins from full thickness to one tenth while plus and minus charges accumulate on the plates. The switch opens and the animation pauses with the capacitor charged. Then the switch swings to contact b and the capacitor drives a counter-clockwise current through the resistor for another ten steps, the line thinning again while the plate charges disappear. Finally the switch returns to the open position.
